name: Crew Rules & Fleet
features:
Agreed with the player (their own list, stages 1-3 done; the player is a former ACMI flight attendant: get the rules right). Build ALL of these:

PLAYER FIXES FIRST (player notes 22 Oct; build these before the rest; screenshot of the top bar in .handover/updates/topbar-space.jpg):
F1. HOTEL DOT: the white crew-at-hotel dot on the map stays while ANY crew member is still at that station (resting, waiting for a ticket, between duties of a tour); today it disappears when the duty completes. Remove it only when the last one leaves.
F2. MARKET ALERTS: move the market-alerts toggle (and its pause-on-offer toggle) from Settings into the Market section of the Fleet screen. A new market offer also shows in the TOP BAR WARNING AREA next to the 1×/2×/4× control, the same place and style as the crew-shortage warning (tap → the offer). Settings keeps nothing about it.
F3. SUB-CHARTER RELIABILITY: sub-chartering must hurt reliability noticeably and progressively (a client notices when its flights are flown by someone else): per sub-chartered leg a reliability cost that grows with how many legs were sub-chartered in the last 90 days (e.g. −0.3 for the first few, rising to −1 per leg when a third or more of a contract's legs were sub-chartered), shown on the sub-charter option's chips and in the plain-language card ('Hurts: reliability −2 · the client notices'). Keep the bot in band.
F4. CONTRACT NAMES: no more repetitive 'Thursday series DUS–FUE' / 'Monday series'. Name series after what they are, with variety and real flavour: tour operator programme names ('TUI summer programme Düsseldorf–Fuerteventura', 'Jet2 weekend rotation', 'Sunweb ski charters Amsterdam–Salzburg', 'Corendon Antalya flights'), events, seasons, sports, the client's own words; the weekday stays in the details, not the title. A big varied pool per archetype; never the same title twice in a row for a client.
F5. CABIN CREW JOIN IN 1 WEEK: hiring flight attendants (PUR/CC — v0.7.2 ranks) takes ~7 days to join (pilots keep their longer lead). Update the hire modal text, bot and balance.
F6. CABIN REFITS START STRAIGHT AWAY: a refit can start as soon as the aircraft is free (no 7-day hangar lead; the first offered slot is the next free window from today, not weeks out); the refit modal lists the earliest slots first and says plainly why a later date is needed if the aircraft is busy.
F7. UP NEXT MORE COMPACT: smaller panel; remove the legend under it (each row already names its type); rows closer together in a tidy grid with thin horizontal AND vertical divider lines (time | flight/reg | route | type), like a departures board; at most ~5 rows; collapsible.
F8. TOP BAR LIVE STRIP (player asked for suggestions; build this default, they can refine): use the empty space between the speed control and cash (see screenshot) for a calm live OPS STRIP: warnings first on the left (crew shortage, market offer, AOG — existing), then compact live facts: 'Airborne 3/5' (aircraft in the air of fleet), 'Next: AWQ717 LHR→CGN in 1:20', 'On time today 92%', 'Crew: 14 on duty · 6 at hotels'. Each item taps through to its screen (Map/Schedule/Crew). Updates at most once per game minute, no flicker or scrolling ticker; shrinks gracefully at Safari width (1180×750) by dropping the lowest-priority items.

1. EASA FTL RESEARCH FIRST: before coding, research and write docs/acmi/EASA-FTL.md from the real rules (Regulation (EU) 965/2012 Subpart FTL, ORO.FTL.205 FDP table by report time and sectors, ORO.FTL.210 cumulative limits (60 h/7 d, 110 h/14 d, 190 h/28 d duty, 100 h/28 d and 900 h/yr block (1000 h/calendar yr)), ORO.FTL.235 rest (min 12 h at home / 10 h away, or the preceding duty length if longer; weekly 36 h recovery with 2 local nights within 168 h), split duty, standby, commander's discretion (2 h, 3 h with augmented crew), in-flight rest extensions by rest facility class (class 1 bunk / class 2 seat flat in a separate area / class 3 economy seat with 40° recline, curtain, leg rest) and augmented-crew FDP (CS FTL.1.205: 3 pilots: 14/15/16 h by class; 4 pilots: 15/16/17 h; cabin crew FDP extension with in-flight rest). Same rules for pilots and cabin crew where EASA says so (cabin crew report may be earlier; cabin crew FDP counted from their earlier report). Then make the engine's crew/rules.ts match the researched tables (a REGRESSION-SAFE change: old saves load; the bot stays in band; tests pin the tables). Keep this doc as the reference for every later crew update.

2. CAPTAINS CAN FLY AS FIRST OFFICERS when short staffed and needed (never an FO as captain): the auto-roster only does it when no FO is available, the duty picker lists captains for an FO seat under a 'Captain flying as FO' label; captain pay stays; a small morale hit for the captain when it happens more than twice a month. Shown on the roster/flight sheet as 'CPT (as FO)'.

3. CREW REST COMPARTMENTS: each aircraft type/variant carries whether it was sold with a crew rest compartment (bunks: class 1) — widebodies may have it or not per airframe (market listings and the fleet card show 'Crew rest: bunks / none'); short-haul types never. With a compartment, FDP extends per the EASA class-1 table (augmented crews). Without one, the CABIN CONFIGURATION (v0.7 refit feature) offers 'Crew rest seats': block off the LAST ROW of economy (curtain; class 3) — these seats STILL COUNT as passenger seats and sell when the duty needs no in-flight rest; when a duty needs in-flight rest they are blocked and the sellable seat count drops for that flight (shown on the flight sheet and in contract feasibility). Class 3 gives the smaller extension per the table. The ladder's augmented-crew/ULR approval uses the real class.

4. CABIN CREW RANKS: remove CSD and SCC. Only two cabin ranks: PUR (Purser, senior cabin crew member / SCCM) and CC (junior cabin crew). Every complement has exactly 1 PUR (SCCM) + CC; widebodies may add a second PUR as deputy only if the type's minimum says so. SAVE MIGRATION: existing CSD and SCC crew become PUR; existing pairings/slots/contracts/requirements/offers that mention CSD/SCC are rewritten; nothing is lost; tests load an old save and check it. Rename everywhere in the UI, docs and bot.

5. HIRING FLIGHT ATTENDANTS WITH MULTIPLE TYPES: in the hire screen the aircraft-type choice for cabin crew is a set of TICK BOXES (hold A320 family, A330, 767, 777...), not a dropdown; price and joining time scale with the number of types; the existing 'up to 3 types' rule applies; staffing views show per-type coverage. Pilots keep one type (rating) as today.

6. SELL OWNED AIRCRAFT AND RETURN LEASES EARLY: Fleet card → 'Sell' for owned aircraft with a market value from age, hours/cycles, check status and cabin (quote from the v0.7 market model; sale takes days; cash in; contracts on it must be covered or sub-chartered first — warn). 'Return early' for leased aircraft: early-return fee + return check condition from the v0.7 lease-return feature; the game suggests the LEAST USED aircraft (lowest utilisation last 90 days) when the player asks 'which one?'. Both appear in the fleet list with a plain-language card (v0.7.1 style).

7. REAL-WORLD C-CHECK HUBS: C-checks happen at real MRO hubs by type, not at base (cabin retrofits still happen at home base): e.g. 767 → Miami (ex-euroAtlantic practice), 777 → Amman (Joramco), A330 → France (Bordeaux-Mérignac / Châteauroux), A320 family → Sofia or Malta (Lufthansa Technik), 737 → Budapest or Shannon, A380/A350 → Toulouse / Manila; pick 1–2 per type at your discretion from real MROs, with the hub's price level. The pilots FERRY the aircraft to the hub, DEADHEAD home on commercial flights (shown on the map like other deadheads), and at the end of the check DEADHEAD back to the hub and FERRY the aircraft home — all rostered and costed automatically when a check is booked; the check modal shows the hub, ferry times and the deadhead tickets; A-checks stay at base/line stations as today.

8. 'WHAT'S NEW': already in the game (src/data/whatsNew.ts drives the pop-up, settings.seenWhatsNew, Settings → What's new). Add a v0.7.2 entry at the top with this update's features and improvements in player words.
Keep: calm visuals, iPad landscape, real names, speeds 1/2/4 only, old saves load, bot in band.

BASE: v0.7.1 Crew Control is released and in the tree (Crew Control panel, private jets, plain-language cards/<Term> glossary/WHY? buttons/gauges/timelines). Every new problem this update adds (rest-seat conflicts, captain-as-FO, C-check hub logistics, sale/return, refits) gets the same four-line plain-language card and glossary terms (PUR, crew rest compartment, class 1/3 rest, MRO, dry lease...).
